thread:
incident-bot: ALERT p99 streaming tail latency spike detected in ap-southeast-1 -> eu-west-1 egress path, priority: P1. automated probe shows p99 > 1.2s for streaming tail and increased retransmits :rotating_light:

alex.sre: oncall here, pulling graphs. which services impacted?

marie.net: looks like streaming-gateway and realtime-ingest routes to eu are seeing p95 ~ 350ms, p99 ~ 1.3-1.6s for last 6m. errors are mostly TLS handshake timeouts + connection resets.

raj.network: seeing abnormal SYN retransmit spikes on NAT path from ap-southeast az-b -> transit-gw -> eu-west. likely asymmetric pathing; NAT counters show ephemeral table growing quickly.

alex.sre: tagging network oncall @raj.network, please advise mitigation. CS — any customer-facing noise? @sam.cs

sam.cs: a handful of customers reported degraded live transcripts and streaming stalls. one customer (acme-media) reported ~20% stalled sessions in last 10m, they're escalating.

eva.runtime: can we fallback to smaller response sizes or disable streaming for critical customers? we have a canary flag to force non-streaming fallback.

raj.network: immediate actions: 1) shift egress for affected subnets to alternate NAT cluster in same region (ephemeral port relief) 2) push route steering to avoid the problematic transit hop 3) open support ticket with cloud provider for possible hardware/route flap.

alex.sre: ok do (1) and (2). marie, can you validate SLO break impact after shift? eva, prep rollout for streaming->polling flag for high-impact customers.

marie.net: running pre/post metrics. will watch p95/p99 and retransmit rate.

raj.network: config snippet I'll run on the routing plane (short):
```
# pseudo-config - change egress pool for /24s
set route-policy source 10.12.0.0/16 prefer-nat-pool alt-nat-2
commit
```

raj.network: applying now, might take up to 30s to converge.

deploy-bot: route-change deployment started by raj.network — job id 87233.

alex.sre: paging cadence: 30s checks. marie, call out when p99 drops below 700ms. also update incident channel.

marie.net: initial after-shift snapshot: p95 ~ 220ms, p99 ~ 680ms, retransmits down ~70%. still a few TLS handshake timeouts but trending down.

sam.cs: notifying acme-media with mitigation note and ETA for full recovery ~20m. they asked for IPs we moved them to — sending list.

eva.runtime: started feature toggle for acme-media -> non-streaming fallback, will switch if stalls continue. command: `feature-toggle set acme-media streaming false`

raj.network: cloud provider responded: observed transient route flap on provider transit in ap-southeast-1 affecting a subset of egress nodes. they are rerouting traffic. recommended we keep alternate NAT pools active for 1h.

alex.sre: handoff plan — i'll stay on this for 45m then hand to evening oncall if stable. record in incident timeline: cause = provider transit route flap causing asymmetric NAT pressure -> ephemeral exhaustion -> TCP retransmits -> TLS handshake tail spikes -> streaming stalls.

marie.net: running full p95/p99 report and link: https://telemetry.example.com/incident/5067894321 (internal). adding graphs for: streaming-tail, nat-ephemeral, tls-handshake, tx-retransmits.

sam.cs: customers notified: acme-media (partial impact, mitigated), two other customers on ap-southeast (low impact) — CS follow-up scheduled.

alex.sre: postmortem checklist: preserve packet captures for 15min before route change, export NAT counters, annotate deployment/route-change jobs. include timeline with decision points.

raj.network: captured pcap on affected egress node and saved to s3://redwood-incident/5067894321/pcap.pcap. NAT counters snapshot pushed to the same bucket.

marie.net: final metrics at 20m post-mitigation: p99 back to 420ms, retransmits normalized, streaming stalls dropped below 1%. marking incident as mitigated — keeping open for observation window (1h).

alex.sre: thanks everyone. filing incident ticket and will include customer impact notes + remediation + next steps (auto-stabilize by keeping alt nat pool active & escalation to provider).

incident-bot: Incident updated: status -> mitigated (observation). next: postmortem assigned to alex.sre + raj.network + marie.net.

sam.cs: will follow up with acme-media postmortem summary and SLA credit assessment if needed. :mortar_board:

alex.sre: handoff to evening oncall @kira.sre at 5067894399 — handing off with context and links.

kira.sre: acknowledged, taking over observation window.
